issues.description: The Milkable interface method signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the UML/problem statement specifies messageOnMilk():boolean, while the solution (and its implementing classes) use messageOnMilk():String. This creates a hard mismatch for students about what to implement and would break polymorphic usage shown in Main (printing the return value) depending on which spec they follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Align all artifacts to one return type. Either (A) change the problem statement/UML to messageOnMilk():String and remove the 'return true/false' requirement, or (B) change the solution to boolean messageOnMilk() (and update Goat/Seal + Main printing accordingly).

issues.description: Farm.singFarmSongVerse is structurally inconsistent: the template declares it without an Animal parameter (commented out), while the UML/problem statement and the solution require singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal). This can mislead students about the intended method signature and how singFarmSong() should call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` and add the corresponding Animal import/forward reference so it matches the UML and solution.

issues.description: The Milkable interface method is inconsistently specified: the UML/problem statement defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() with a boolean return type (success/failure), but the solution code defines it as returning a String message. This breaks conceptual mapping for students implementing according to the spec and makes it unclear whether the method should report success (boolean) or a textual message (String).
issues.suggestedFix: Align all artifacts on one signature. If following the problem/UML, change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return boolean in solution (and update Seal/Goat + Main accordingly). Alternatively, if String messages are intended, update the UML/problem statement text to specify String return type and remove the success/failure boolean requirement.

issues.description: The template Farm.singFarmSongVerse method stub omits the Animal parameter (commented as /*Animal animal*/), while the problem statement and solution both define singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal). This creates a naming/signature mismatch that can confuse students about the intended method signature when completing the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` (and add/import Animal as needed) to match the problem statement/UML and the intended implementation.
